questions.question_text: The most frequent symptom of schizophrenia is:
questions.explanation: Lack of insight is a symptom in 97% of cases of schizophrenia, auditory hallucinations in 74%.

questions.question_text: Schneiderian first-rank symptoms include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: First-rank symptoms occur in other psychoses; they are highly suggestive of schizophrenia but not characteristic of it.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of schizophrenia?

options.text: First-rank symptoms are pathognomonic of schizophrenia
The ICD-10 general criteria for schizophrenia are based on Schneider's first-rank symptoms
The ICD-10 general criteria for schizophrenia require the presence of symptoms and signs lasting for at least 6 months
The prevalence of schizophrenia varies widely in different countries
The DSM-IV-TR diagnostic criteria for schizophrenia require the onset of symptoms between the ages of 15 and 45

correct_answer.text: The ICD-10 general criteria for schizophrenia are based on Schneider's first-rank symptoms

correct_answers.text: The ICD-10 general criteria for schizophrenia are based on Schneider's first-rank symptoms

questions.explanation: ICD-10 general criteria require symptoms for 1 month and DSM-IV for 6 months. The incidence and prevalence are roughly equal in all countries: incidence is 0.17–0.54 per 1000 population and prevalence 1.4–4.6 per 100 population at risk.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true, except:

options.text: The onset of schizophrenia characteristically occurs between the ages of 15 and 45
Well controlled evidence indicates that a specific family pattern plays a causative role in the development of schizophrenia
Schizophrenia is equally prevalent in men and women
Onset of schizophrenia is earlier in men than women
People who develop schizophrenia are more likely to have been born in the winter and early spring

correct_answer.text: Well controlled evidence indicates that a specific family pattern plays a causative role in the development of schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: Well controlled evidence indicates that a specific family pattern plays a causative role in the development of schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Bateson's double-bind theory, Lidz's schisms and skewed families, Wynne's pseudomutual and pseudohostile family theory and expressed emotion theories try to explain family factors in the aetiology, but there is no good evidence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of people suffering from schizophrenia?

options.text: A higher mortality rate from accidents and natural causes is observed
Men have lower social class distribution than their fathers
Men are more likely to drift into inner-city areas

questions.explanation: These are all features of the social drift theory of schizophrenia developed by Goldberg and Morrison (1963). Goldberg EM, Morrison SL. Shizophrenia and social class. Br J Psychiatry 1963; 109: 785–802.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding research evidence in the aetiology of schizophrenia?

options.text: A positive correlation between high pre-treatment central nervous system concentration of homovanillic acid and the severity of psychotic symptoms is observed
Agonistic activity at the serotonin 5-HT 2receptor reduces psychotic symptoms
There is an increase in the size of the limbic area in patients with schizophrenia
The changes in regional brain volume in patients with schizophrenia show a clear association with gender
Movement disorders unrelated to antipsychotic drug treatment have been more associated with late-onset illness

correct_answer.text: A positive correlation between high pre-treatment central nervous system concentration of homovanillic acid and the severity of psychotic symptoms is observed

correct_answers.text: A positive correlation between high pre-treatment central nervous system concentration of homovanillic acid and the severity of psychotic symptoms is observed

questions.explanation: 5-HT 2antagonism reduces psychosis; there is a decrease in the size of the limbic area; movement disorders are more associated with early-onset illness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most frequent behavioural abnormality associated with schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Social withdrawal occurs in 74% of cases of schizophrenia, neglect of appearance in 30%, sexually unusual behaviour in 8% and suicide attempts in 4%.

questions.question_text: Regarding clinical features of schizophrenia, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: In acute schizophrenia, orientation is usually impaired
Depressive symptoms in schizophrenia may be a response to recovery of insight
About 50% of patients with acute schizophrenia experience acute depressive symptomatology
Water intoxication is associated with schizophrenia
The social background of the patient may affect content of symptoms

correct_answer.text: In acute schizophrenia, orientation is usually impaired

correct_answers.text: In acute schizophrenia, orientation is usually impaired

questions.explanation: In acute schizophrenia, orientation is usually normal, but it is recognized that generalized deficits in cognitive function occur.

questions.question_text: Which of the following types of hallucinations occur in schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Auditory hallucination is the most frequent one. All other types are reported only rarely.

questions.question_text: All of the following are regarded as aetiologically related to schizophrenia, except:
questions.explanation: Among schizotypal criteria, eccentricity, affect constriction and excessive social anxiety are linked to schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man was brought to the hospital for his ninth admission, the first one being at the age of 16. He was observed to have a child-like quality to his speech and manner and he walks with an exaggerated hip movement. His speech is incoherent and his behaviour is disorganized. He also had some fleeting and fragmentary delusions and hallucinations. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: The onset of hebephrenic schizophrenia (disorganized type in DSM-IV) is usually before 25 years of age.

questions.question_text: Regarding subtypes of schizophrenia as classified in ICD-10, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: In paranoid schizophrenia, disturbances of affect and catatonic symptoms are relatively inconspicuous
Hebephrenia should normally be diagnosed only in adolescents or young adults
Episodes of violent excitement may be a striking feature of catatonic schizophrenia
A depressive state with florid and prominent schizophrenic symptoms is characteristic of post-schizophrenic depression
Chronic undifferentiated schizophrenia is classified under residual schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: A depressive state with florid and prominent schizophrenic symptoms is characteristic of post-schizophrenic depression

correct_answers.text: A depressive state with florid and prominent schizophrenic symptoms is characteristic of post-schizophrenic depression

questions.explanation: Either positive or negative symptoms must be present but they should not dominate the clinical picture. If these symptoms are florid and prominent, the diagnosis should remain of the appropriate schizophrenia subtype.

questions.question_text: Regarding prognosis of schizophrenia, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Increased relapse rate is associated with a high expressed emotion in the family
Family history of affective disorder is a predictor of good prognosis
Later onset is a good prognostic indicator
High educational attainment is protective against a high risk of suicide

correct_answer.text: High educational attainment is protective against a high risk of suicide

correct_answers.text: High educational attainment is protective against a high risk of suicide

questions.explanation: High educational attainment increases the risk.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about delusional disorder is true?

options.text: Erotomanic type is a subtype in DSM-IV
It is more common in men
Mean age of onset is earlier in females
It is more common when there is an increased family history of schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: Erotomanic type is a subtype in DSM-IV

correct_answers.text: Erotomanic type is a subtype in DSM-IV

questions.explanation: There is an equal sex ratio or a slightly higher prevalence in females; the mean age of onset is 35 in men, 45 in women; it is more common when there is an increased family history of psychiatric problems; personality is preserved.

questions.question_text: A 64-year-old man admitted on the ward has delusions that all his wealth has gone. He also believes that his organs are decaying and that people hate him because of the smell of his rotten body parts. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Nihilistic delusions occur.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old woman on the ward believes that her daughter has been replaced by a double. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Capgras syndrome is the delusion that a close relative has been replaced by an identical-looking impostor.

questions.question_text: Regarding delusional syndromes, which of the following is true?

options.text: Erotomania is more common in males
Capgras syndrome is more common in males
Pathological jealousy is more common in males
Induced psychosis (folie à deux) involves members of the same family only
The primary cause of Capgras syndrome is always an organic brain dysfunction

correct_answer.text: Pathological jealousy is more common in males

correct_answers.text: Pathological jealousy is more common in males

questions.explanation: Erotomania is also known as de Clérambault's syndrome.

questions.question_text: In ICD-10:

options.text: Schizotypal disorder and schizoid personality disorder are classified separately
The presence of occasional or transitory auditory hallucinations, particularly in elderly patients, rules out the diagnosis of delusional disorder
Delusional dysmorphophobia is classified under 'Other schizophrenia'
If acute and transient psychotic disorder persists for more than 72 hours, a change in diagnosis is necessary
Mood-incongruent psychotic symptoms in affective disorders by themselves justify a diagnosis of schizoaffective disorder

correct_answer.text: Schizotypal disorder and schizoid personality disorder are classified separately

correct_answers.text: Schizotypal disorder and schizoid personality disorder are classified separately

questions.explanation: Delusional dysmorphophobia is classified under 'Other persistent delusional disorders'; acute and transient psychotic disorder develops in less than 2 weeks.

questions.question_text: Disorientation is commonly associated with:
questions.explanation: In delirium tremens, major withdrawal (hallucinations) occurs 10–72 hours after the last drink. The signs and symptoms include visual and auditory hallucinations, whole body tremor, vomiting, diaphoresis and hypertension.

questions.question_text: All of the following are associated with acute intoxication from cannabinoids, except:
questions.explanation: Nystagmus occurs in acute intoxication with alcohol.

questions.question_text: According to ICD-10, a diagnosis of substance dependence syndrome can be made if all of the following are present, except:

options.text: A sense of compulsion to take the substance
Persistent substance use despite clear evidence of harmful consequences

questions.explanation: A physiological withdrawal state is necessary.

questions.question_text: Features of delirium include:
questions.explanation: Other features of delirium include impairment of immediate recall and recent memory, and disorientation in time, place or person.

questions.question_text: All of the following are causes of delirium, except:
questions.explanation: In catatonic schizophrenia, a dreamlike (oneiroid) state occurs, with vivid scenic hallucinations, but it is not delirium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of schizophrenia-like states in elderly people?

options.text: They can be aetiologically associated with sensory deprivation
They are more common in males
They are mostly associated with a family history of schizophrenia
They are characteristically associated with visual hallucinations
They respond well to antipsychotics, with remission of symptoms in 90% of cases

correct_answer.text: They can be aetiologically associated with sensory deprivation

correct_answers.text: They can be aetiologically associated with sensory deprivation

questions.explanation: The female:male ratio is 7:1; the most common hallucination is auditory; 50–75% of patients respond to antipsychotics, with full or partial remission.

questions.question_text: Regarding the relationship between schizophrenia and affective disorder, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: At least one-third of schizophrenics have depressive symptoms
There is an increased occurrence of affective disorder in family members of schizophrenics
Bipolar disorder is more common in families of schizoaffective disorder patients than those of schizophrenia patients
Bipolar disorder is more common in male relatives of schizophrenics
Unipolar disorder is more common in female relatives of schizophrenics

correct_answer.text: Bipolar disorder is more common in families of schizoaffective disorder patients than those of schizophrenia patients

correct_answers.text: Bipolar disorder is more common in families of schizoaffective disorder patients than those of schizophrenia patients

questions.explanation: Bipolar disorder is equal in both.

questions.question_text: Delirium tremens:

options.text: Carries a significant risk of mortality
Has symptoms that characteristically are worse at night
Is associated with dilation of pupils and prolonged insomnia

questions.explanation: Despite appropriate treatment, the current mortality for patients with delirium tremens ranges from 5 to 15%. Mortality was as high as 35% prior to the era of intensive care and advanced pharmacotherapy. The most common conditions leading to death in these patients are respiratory failure and cardiac arrhythmias.

questions.question_text: Chronic alcohol misuse:

options.text: Causes medial thalamic lesions leading to amnesia
Causes up to a six-fold increase in the suicide rate
Is associated with erectile and ejaculatory dysfunction

questions.explanation: Chronic alcohol misuse is associated with alcoholic dementia, personality deterioration, mood disorder, suicidal behaviour, impaired psychosexual function, pathological jealousy and alcoholic hallucinosis.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about alcohol dependence, except:

options.text: It may be mediated by dopamine release in mesolimbic pathways
It is increasingly observed in antisocial personality disorder
It is more common in Asians with decreased function of aldehyde dehydrogenase
It is associated with increased blood pressure

correct_answer.text: It is more common in Asians with decreased function of aldehyde dehydrogenase

correct_answers.text: It is more common in Asians with decreased function of aldehyde dehydrogenase

questions.explanation: Decreased function of aldehyde dehydrogenase causes an unpleasant reaction and reduces alcohol misuse.

questions.question_text: Pathological jealousy occurs in:
questions.explanation: Disorders associated with pathological jealousy are schizophrenia, mood disorder, organic disorder, substance misuse (including alcohol) and personality disorder.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about narcolepsy, except:

options.text: It is more frequent in females
Sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations occur in 75% of patients
There is a family history in one-third of patients

correct_answer.text: Sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations occur in 75% of patients

correct_answers.text: Sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations occur in 75% of patients

questions.explanation: Sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations occur in 25% of patients.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of transient global amnesia?

options.text: It commonly occurs in adolescents and young adults
It occurs as sudden onset of global amnesia
It is associated with localized perfusion abnormalities in the brain, observed on functional imaging
It is usually associated with abnormalities on neurological examination
The patient usually recovers, with amnesia of the period affected, but recurrence is common

correct_answer.text: It is associated with localized perfusion abnormalities in the brain, observed on functional imaging

correct_answers.text: It is associated with localized perfusion abnormalities in the brain, observed on functional imaging

questions.explanation: Localized perfusion abnormalities in the brain occur in middle and later life with isolated anterograde amnesia, and recurrence is rare.

questions.question_text: Klüver–Bucy syndrome includes all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Hypersexuality is a feature of Kluver–Bucy syndrome.

questions.question_text: All of the following are common symptoms of temporal lobe epilepsy, except:
questions.explanation: Pareidolic illusions occur in normal people; temporal lobe epilepsy is also provoked by psychomimetic drugs (images are seen from shapes).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of pseudodementia?

options.text: It is most common in elderly depressed patients
'Don't know' responses and poor involvement on neuropsychological tests are characteristic
It can be caused by conversion disorder
When it is caused by a factitious disorder, a source of secondary gain may be apparent

questions.explanation: Although pseudodementia commonly occurs in depressed elderly patients, it is important to understand that depression can feature early in the course of dementia as well.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true of frontotemporal dementia, except:

options.text: It is more common in young-onset dementias
When caused by Pick's disease, knife-blade atrophy is common

questions.explanation: Relatively preserved memory early on is characteristic of frontotemporal dementia.

questions.question_text: Clinical manifestations of idiopathic Parkinson's disease include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Resting tremor is a clinical manifestation in idiopathic Parkinson's disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are characteristic of Huntington's disease?

options.text: Purposeless fidgeting choreiform movements occur, which the patient may attempt to disguise
It has low rates of affective disorders
Predictive genetic testing is not currently available

correct_answer.text: Purposeless fidgeting choreiform movements occur, which the patient may attempt to disguise

correct_answers.text: Purposeless fidgeting choreiform movements occur, which the patient may attempt to disguise

questions.explanation: Huntington's disease occurs typically in middle age; it is autosomal dominant with complete penetrance; it features higher rates of depression, bipolar disorder and schizophrenia; genetic testing for the causative mutation (DNA triplet repeat coding for glutamine) is now widely available.

questions.question_text: Subdural haematoma:

options.text: Usually lacks a history of head injury
Is often associated with hemiparesis and oculomotor signs
Surgical evacuation may reverse the symptoms

questions.explanation: Acute subdural haematoma (SDH – a collection of blood over the surface of the brain) is the most common type of traumatic intracranial haematoma, occurring in 24% of patients who present comatose. SDHs are usually caused by trauma but can be spontaneous or caused by a procedure such as lumbar puncture. Anticoagulation, such as with heparin or warfarin, may be a contributing factor.

questions.question_text: Regarding prion diseases, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease is the most common
Sporadic disease accounts for less than 50% of cases
Kuru is transmitted by ritual cannibalism
Gerstmann–Straussler–Scheinker syndrome is an autosomal dominantly inherited prion disease
They are caused by abnormal fibrillar prion glycoprotein deposition in the brain

correct_answer.text: Sporadic disease accounts for less than 50% of cases

correct_answers.text: Sporadic disease accounts for less than 50% of cases

questions.explanation: Prion diseases or transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (TSEs) are a family of rare progressive neurodegenerative disorders that affect both humans and animals. Human prion diseases are Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (CJD), variant Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (vCJD), Gerstmann–Straussler–Scheinker syndrome, fatal familial insomnia and kuru.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (CJD) are correct, except:

options.text: Sporadic CJD affects both sexes equally
Sporadic CJD presents typically between 60 and 65 years
Sporadic CJD is usually heralded by cognitive decline
Variant CJD is linked with bovine spongiform encephalopathy
It often progresses to death within several years

correct_answer.text: It often progresses to death within several years

correct_answers.text: It often progresses to death within several years

questions.explanation: Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease often progresses to death within 6 months.

questions.question_text: A 73-year-old man has been referred to the memory clinic with a history of memory problems over the last 6 months. He presents with a broad-based small-stepped gait with difficulty in initiation, and slowing in response. His wife reported that he has developed urinary incontinence recently. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: In normal-pressure hydrocephalus, the presence of hippocampal atrophy indicates associated Alzheimer's disease, with a poor response to shunting.

questions.question_text: A 58-year-old man presented to the memory assessment service with a history of personality changes over the last 12 months with progressive impairment in his language function. He was observed to have paralysis of the extra-ocular muscles, dysarthria, cervical and truncal dystonia and ataxia. The most probable diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a rare degenerative disease of the brain. The disease impairs movements and balance. Many people with PSP also experience changes in mood, behaviour and personality.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of alcohol?

options.text: It produces its effects in the brain mainly through action on NMDA receptors
At higher levels it can cause death secondary to respiratory depression and aspiration
Its use is associated with increased REM sleep and stage 4 sleep
It is associated with elevation of g-GT in a minor proportion of people with alcohol-related disorders
Carbohydrate-deficient transferrin is identified as a biomarker for chronic alcoholism with high sensitivity and low specificity

correct_answer.text: At higher levels it can cause death secondary to respiratory depression and aspiration

correct_answers.text: At higher levels it can cause death secondary to respiratory depression and aspiration

questions.explanation: No single molecular target has been identified to mediate the effects of alcohol. Its use is associated with decreased REM and stage 4 sleep; g-GT is elevated in 80% of people with alcohol-related disorders; carbohydrate-deficient transferrin is identified as a biomarker for chronic alcoholism with high sensitivity and low specificity.

questions.question_text: Foetal alcohol syndrome includes:
questions.explanation: Intrauterine exposure to alcohol results in foetal alcohol syndrome.

questions.question_text: Postnatal blues:

options.text: Are characterized by tearfulness, emotional lability and confusion
Peak at the third to fifth days postpartum
Are aetiologically linked to progesterone withdrawal after delivery

questions.explanation: Postnatal blues are more frequent among primigravida women.

questions.question_text: Puerperal psychosis is characterized by all of the following, except:

options.text: Gradual onset within the first 2 months of childbirth

correct_answer.text: Gradual onset within the first 2 months of childbirth

correct_answers.text: Gradual onset within the first 2 months of childbirth

questions.explanation: Puerperal psychosis is characterized by abrupt onset, within the first 2 weeks of childbirth.

questions.question_text: All of the following are correct about erectile dysfunction, except:

options.text: It is organic in about 90% of cases
It can be caused by Peyronie's disease
Hyperprolactinaemia secondary to alcoholism can be a cause
Naltrexone therapy improves impotence of apparent non-organic cause
Alpha-adrenergic blockers are not usually associated with erectile dysfunction but may cause ejaculatory failure

correct_answer.text: It is organic in about 90% of cases

correct_answers.text: It is organic in about 90% of cases

questions.explanation: Erectile dysfunction is organic in about 50% of cases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of night terrors:

options.text: They occur during stage 3 and 4 sleep
They usually occur 1 or 2 hours after sleep starts
There is little recall the following morning
Enuresis may occur during an episode

questions.explanation: Night terror disorder is sometimes familial, and begins and ends in childhood, though it occasionally persists into adult life.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of delirium?

options.text: It affects 10–25% of over-65-year-olds admitted to medical wards
It is more marked in conditions with poor illumination
Mortality can be up to 30–40% because of the underlying condition

questions.explanation: In patients who are admitted with delirium, mortality rates are 10–26%.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true of late-onset psychosis, except:

options.text: It is more common in females
40–45% of cases present with Schneiderian first-rank symptoms
80% of cases present with visual hallucinations
Sensory impairment is associated with development of paranoid symptoms
About a quarter of patients show full response to treatment

correct_answer.text: 80% of cases present with visual hallucinations

correct_answers.text: 80% of cases present with visual hallucinations

questions.explanation: Some hallucinatory experiences can be present in up to 80% of cases, but auditory hallucinations are most common.
